Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're starting the internal design for our PrivateHost (VPC) rollout and have two immediate blockers we need to resolve before the network team will approve the architecture:

1) DNS delegation model for internal FQDNs (split-horizon vs delegated subzones). We need a pattern that allows our internal resolver to handoff to Redwood's private endpoint names without leaking records to public DNS.

2) Certificate provisioning for the edge proxy in our air-gapped region — ACME doesn't work in the current setup, and our security team requires mTLS between the edge proxy and the Redwood runtime.

Can you sketch possible approaches and call out trade-offs (who owns zone delegation, how cert rotation can be automated, and what the handshake looks like for mTLS termination)? We're aiming for an architecture doc we can attach to our change request by 11/29.

Subject: Re: PrivateHost deployment constraints and DNS options

Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. High level proposals below; I sketch trade-offs and follow-up questions.

Option A — Delegated private subzone (recommended when tenant controls DNS infrastructure):
- Acme creates a private subzone (e.g. redwood.acme.internal) delegated to Redwood's internal nameservers in the VPC via conditional forwarders.
- Pros: Redwood controls records for service endpoints; no public leakage; easy to map SNI to internal endpoints.
- Cons: Requires network policy changes to allow conditional forwarding and controlled DNS TTLs; rotation of NS records must be coordinated.

Option B — Split-horizon authoritative split at resolver level:
- Acme maintains same zone name internally but uses a split-horizon config where internal zone includes records for redwood-hosted endpoints and external zone does not.
- Pros: No new zone names for customers; existing service discovery remains unchanged.
- Cons: More operational overhead for Acme; harder for us to make schema changes without change control; risk of record drift.

mTLS & certificate options:
1) Internal CA + short-lived certs (recommended for air-gapped): use your PKI to issue edge certs with SANs for the delegated FQDNs. Provide a CSR template and an automation script (or stateful cert bundle) for rotation.
2) Vault/PKI (if available): Acme runs HashiVault/Entrust in-air-gap, we integrate via SCEP/EST or offline CSR signing.
3) Manual/long-lived wildcard: acceptable as stopgap but increases blast radius and is noncompliant with your rotation policy.

ACME note: ACME challenges that require outbound reachability (http-01, tls-alpn-01) won't work in strict air-gapped setups. dns-01 can work if Acme's DNS provider supports API access from an allowed jumpbox.

Questions for your network/security teams:
- Can we provision a small conditional forwarder from your VPC resolvers to an internal Redwood resolver?
- Do you have an offline CA/Vault we can integrate for CSR signing?
- What's your maximum acceptable cert TTL (days)?

I'll assemble a one-page handoff playbook and a checklist. Looping Laura for ops-sre requirements on our side.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding SRE/ops perspective — a few implementation details we should lock before change window: 

- TLS termination point: we prefer mTLS to terminate at the edge proxy, then mutual-auth the connection to the runtime via an internal client cert (reduces double-termination risks). Edge proxy will present a cert to clients; runtime nodes will require client certs.
- SANs & Subject constraints: certs should include both the delegated FQDN (edge.example.redwood.acme) and internal node names used for health checks. Avoid wildcard certs unless your policy permits OCSP stapling tests to be skipped.
- Rotation automation: our dedicated deployment supports a webhook-based rotation flow — Acme's CA can push signed certs to a secure S3 bucket (VPC-accessible) and we pull them into the edge proxies. For fully air-gapped, exchange signed bundles via secure file transfer and we provide a rotation script.
- Health probes: ensure the internal probes use SNI to match cert SANs; otherwise probe failures will look like cert errors.

Action items for Acme team:
- Provide the person who can approve conditional forwarder changes and a point of contact for on-prem PKI (name/email).
- Confirm whether HashiCorp Vault or an equivalent will be used. If yes, share API endpoints or an offline CSR workflow.

Laura
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference

Fwd-ing a note from our on-prem team — we did something similar for another customer and the two practical pitfalls were:

1) DNS TTLs set too low caused excessive propagation churn when we rotated proxy IPs; solution: coordinate a 300s min TTL and schedule rotations in maintenance windows.
2) Certificate chain validation failing on the runtime due to missing intermediate CA in the bundle. Make sure the edge cert bundle includes full chain and that runtime trust stores include the issuing intermediate.

Also, if Acme cannot run conditional forwarding, consider using an internal forwarding appliance: it can act as DNS proxy and forward only the redwood.* subdomain to our resolvers while leaving the rest untouched. That often avoids touching their authoritative server configs.

-David
David Smith
Infrastructure Consultant

Hi all — attaching a concise handoff playbook and checklist for the change control request. Summary of the chosen approach and immediate next steps below.

Chosen approach (consensus):
- Delegated private subzone (redwood.acme.internal) via a resolvable conditional forwarder to Redwood's VPC resolver. This gives us control of endpoint records while keeping zone private.
- Certificate model: Acme will sign edge proxy CSRs with their internal CA. Redwood will require full cert bundles (leaf + intermediates) and provide an automated upload endpoint for rotation if a network path exists; otherwise we will use secure file transfer for the initial rollout and quarterly rotation.
- mTLS: Edge proxy authenticates clients with client certs; backend runtime requires client certs from the proxy. We'll use short-lived certs (recommended 7–14 days) where automation is available.

Immediate next steps:
- Sarah: confirm the DNS approver and provide maintenance window availability by 2026-12-06.
- Acme PKI: send CSR signing contact and a test signed bundle (expires >30 days). Location: secure S3 path (details in attached checklist) or SFTP contact.
- Neha/Laura: we will schedule a dry-run in our staging VPC next week and validate probe configuration and rotation scripts.
